subproblem.title: Hⁿ-a.e. point of a Lipschitz image has only Lebesgue-density-point preimages
subproblem.statement: Let n, ℓ ∈ ℕ, ℝⁿ := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) with Lebesgue measure Lⁿ (volume), E := Ambient n ℓ = ℝ^{n+ℓ}, Hⁿ := μHE[n] on E, let C ⊆ ℝⁿ be a Borel set and F : ℝⁿ → E a Lipschitz map. Then for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ E, every w ∈ C with F(w) = x is a Lebesgue density point of C: Lⁿ(C ∩ B_r(w))/Lⁿ(B_r(w)) → 1 as r ↓ 0 (closed balls, quotient in [0, ∞]).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (C : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n))) (F : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) → Ambient n ℓ), MeasurableSet C → (∃ K : NNReal, LipschitzWith K F) → ∀ᵐ x ∂(μHE[n] : Measure (Ambient n ℓ)), ∀ w ∈ C, F w = x → Tendsto (fun r : ℝ ↦ volume (C ∩ closedBall w r) / volume (closedBall w r)) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 1)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 3 of the parent proof (density points; Lebesgue density theorem and the Lipschitz image estimate). No errata apply.

Notation. ℝⁿ := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) with Lebesgue measure Lⁿ = volume; E := Ambient n ℓ; Hⁿ := μHE[n] on E; B_r(w) := closed ball; for w ∈ ℝⁿ let q_w(r) := Lⁿ(C ∩ B_r(w))/Lⁿ(B_r(w)) ∈ [0, ∞].

1. Lebesgue density theorem. ℝⁿ is a finite-dimensional normed space, so it has the Besicovitch covering property, and Lⁿ is locally finite. By Mathlib Besicovitch.ae_tendsto_measure_inter_div (with the measure Lⁿ and the set C), for Lⁿ⌞C-almost every w, q_w(r) → 1 as r ↓ 0.

2. The non-density points are Lⁿ-null. Let P := {w ∈ ℝⁿ : q_w(r) does not tend to 1 as r ↓ 0} and Z := P ∩ C. Step 1 says (Lⁿ⌞C)(P) = 0. Since C is Borel, (Lⁿ⌞C)(P) = Lⁿ(P ∩ C) (Measure.restrict_apply'), so Lⁿ(Z) = 0.

3. Their image is Hⁿ-null. Let κ ≥ 0 be a Lipschitz constant of F. By the Lipschitz image estimate for Hausdorff measure (Simon Ch. 2, 1.8(i); SimonGMT Chapter02.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image_le_of_lipschitzOn, applied to F, which is κ-Lipschitz on Z), Hⁿ(F(Z)) ≤ κⁿ·μHE[n](Z), where μHE[n] on ℝⁿ equals Lⁿ (Mathlib EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume). Hence Hⁿ(F(Z)) ≤ κⁿ·Lⁿ(Z) = 0.

4. Conclusion. Suppose x ∈ E violates the conclusion, i.e. there is w ∈ C with F(w) = x such that q_w(r) does not tend to 1. Then w ∈ P ∩ C = Z, so x = F(w) ∈ F(Z). Hence the set of points violating the conclusion is contained in the Hⁿ-null set F(Z) (it need not be measurable; it is contained in a null set), and the conclusion holds for Hⁿ-almost every x ∈ E. ∎

subproblem.title: Lusin compact exhaustion of a finite-measure set in ℝ^{n+ℓ}
subproblem.statement: Let n, ℓ ∈ ℕ, E := Ambient n ℓ = ℝ^{n+ℓ} with its Borel σ-algebra, μ any measure on E, A ⊆ E a μ-null-measurable set with μ(A) < ∞, and g : E → ℝ a function that is a.e.-strongly measurable with respect to μ⌞A. Then there are compact sets K_k ⊆ A (k ∈ ℕ) such that g restricted to each K_k is continuous (ContinuousOn g K_k) and μ(A ∖ ⋃_k K_k) = 0.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Ambient n ℓ)) (A : Set (Ambient n ℓ)) (g : Ambient n ℓ → ℝ), NullMeasurableSet A μ → μ A ≠ ⊤ → AEStronglyMeasurable g (μ.restrict A) → ∃ K : ℕ → Set (Ambient n ℓ), (∀ k, IsCompact (K k) ∧ K k ⊆ A ∧ ContinuousOn g (K k)) ∧ μ (A \ ⋃ k, K k) = 0
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 5 of the parent proof (construction of the Lusin pieces), stated for an arbitrary measure and an arbitrary finite-measure set. In the parent's application A = M ∩ F(C) already has finite Hⁿ-measure (step 2 of the parent proof: Hⁿ(F(C)) ≤ κⁿLⁿ(C) < ∞), so the truncation {θ̃ ≥ 1/q} used there only to obtain finiteness is not needed; the truncation to closed balls B_q(0), which gives compactness, is kept. Lusin's theorem is Simon Ch. 1, 1.17. No errata apply.

Notation. E := Ambient n ℓ (a finite-dimensional normed space, so closed bounded sets are compact), B_q(0) := closed ball of radius q about 0, μ⌞S := μ restricted to S.

1. Borel core of A. Since A is μ-null-measurable, there is a Borel set A' ⊆ A with A' = A μ-almost everywhere (Mathlib NullMeasurableSet.exists_measurable_subset_ae_eq); in particular μ(A ∖ A') = 0.

2. Borel version of g. Since g is a.e.-strongly measurable for μ⌞A, there is a strongly measurable, hence Borel measurable, g̃: E → ℝ with g = g̃ μ⌞A-almost everywhere (AEStronglyMeasurable.mk). The set {y : g(y) ≠ g̃(y)} is therefore μ⌞A-null; let S be its measurable hull with respect to μ⌞A (toMeasurable): S is Borel, contains {g ≠ g̃}, and (μ⌞A)(S) = 0.

3. μ(A' ∩ S) = 0. The set A' ∩ S is Borel and contained in A (A' ⊆ A), so μ(A' ∩ S) = μ((A' ∩ S) ∩ A) = (μ⌞A)(A' ∩ S) ≤ (μ⌞A)(S) = 0.

4. The good set. Let A'' := A' ∖ S. Then A'' is Borel, A'' ⊆ A, and g(y) = g̃(y) for every y ∈ A'' (because y ∉ S ⊇ {g ≠ g̃}). Moreover A ∖ A'' ⊆ (A ∖ A') ∪ (A' ∩ S): a point of A not in A'' either is not in A' or lies in A' ∩ S. By steps 1 and 3, μ(A ∖ A'') = 0.

5. Lusin pieces. Fix q, m ∈ ℕ and put B_q := A'' ∩ B_q(0), a Borel set with μ(B_q) ≤ μ(A) < ∞. The restricted measure ν_q := μ⌞B_q is a finite Borel measure on the metric space E, hence weakly regular (Mathlib WeaklyRegular.of_pseudoMetrizableSpace_of_isFiniteMeasure); in particular, for every Borel set S' and every δ > 0 there is a closed F ⊆ S' with ν_q(S' ∖ F) < δ (MeasurableSet.exists_isClosed_sdiff_lt). This is exactly the regularity hypothesis of Lusin's theorem in the form SimonGMT Chapter01.exists_isClosed_continuousOn_of_measurable, which we apply to the measure ν_q, the Borel set B_q (ν_q(B_q) < ∞), the Borel function g̃ and ε := 1/(m + 1) > 0: there is a closed set C_{q,m} ⊆ B_q with ν_q(B_q ∖ C_{q,m}) < 1/(m + 1) such that g̃ restricted to C_{q,m} is continuous. Since B_q ∖ C_{q,m} is Borel and contained in B_q, ν_q(B_q ∖ C_{q,m}) = μ(B_q ∖ C_{q,m}); thus μ(B_q ∖ C_{q,m}) < 1/(m + 1).

6. Properties of the pieces. C_{q,m} is closed and contained in the compact ball B_q(0), hence compact. C_{q,m} ⊆ B_q ⊆ A'' ⊆ A. Since g = g̃ on A'' ⊇ C_{q,m}, the restriction of g to C_{q,m} coincides with that of g̃, so g restricted to C_{q,m} is continuous.

7. Covering. For each q ∈ ℕ and every m ∈ ℕ, μ(B_q ∖ ⋃_{m'} C_{q,m'}) ≤ μ(B_q ∖ C_{q,m}) < 1/(m + 1); letting m → ∞ gives μ(B_q ∖ ⋃_{m'} C_{q,m'}) = 0. Now let y ∈ A ∖ ⋃_{q,m} C_{q,m}. If y ∉ A'', then y ∈ A ∖ A''. If y ∈ A'', choose q ∈ ℕ with q ≥ |y|; then y ∈ B_q and y ∉ ⋃_{m} C_{q,m}. Hence A ∖ ⋃_{q,m} C_{q,m} ⊆ (A ∖ A'') ∪ ⋃_{q∈ℕ} (B_q ∖ ⋃_m C_{q,m}), a countable union of μ-null sets (step 4 and the first sentence of this step), so μ(A ∖ ⋃_{q,m} C_{q,m}) = 0.

8. Indexing by ℕ. For k ∈ ℕ let K_k := C_{q,m} with (q, m) := Nat.unpair k. Each K_k is one of the sets C_{q,m}, so it is compact, contained in A, and g restricted to K_k is continuous (step 6). Every C_{q,m} equals K_{Nat.pair q m} because Nat.unpair (Nat.pair q m) = (q, m); hence ⋃_{q,m} C_{q,m} ⊆ ⋃_k K_k and μ(A ∖ ⋃_k K_k) ≤ μ(A ∖ ⋃_{q,m} C_{q,m}) = 0. ∎

subproblem.statement: Let n, ℓ ∈ ℕ, E := Ambient n ℓ = ℝ^{n+ℓ}, Hⁿ := μHE[n], and let a = (M, θ) be an admissible pair (a : RectifiablePair n ℓ: M is countably n-rectifiable and Hⁿ-null-measurable, θ(y) > 0 for y ∈ M, and θ is Hⁿ-integrable on M ∩ K for every compact K ⊆ E). Let μ := (mk a).weight be the weight of V = v(M, θ). Then (i) μ(K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ E (IsFiniteMeasureOnCompacts μ), and (ii) for every function g : E → ℝ, ∫ g dμ = ∫_M θ(y)·g(y) dHⁿ(y) (Bochner integrals, a non-integrable function having integral 0; the identity holds for all g).

Source: step 1 of the parent proof (Simon Ch. 4, 1.1: μ_V = Hⁿ⌞θ), with all details filled in. No errata apply.

Notation. E := Ambient n ℓ, Hⁿ := μHE[n] on E, B_k(0) := closed ball of radius k about 0, ofReal(s) := max(s, 0) ∈ [0, ∞) for s ∈ ℝ, μ := (mk a).weight, M := a.M, θ := a.θ.

1. Unfolding the weight. By definition (mk a).weight = Quot.lift (b ↦ pairWeight n b.M b.θ) _ (Quot.mk _ a), and Quot.lift applied to Quot.mk a reduces definitionally to the lifted function at a. Hence μ = pairWeight n M θ = (Hⁿ⌞M).withDensity ρ with ρ(y) := ofReal(θ(y)) ∈ [0, ∞).

2. θ is a.e.-strongly measurable for Hⁿ⌞M. Every y ∈ E lies in B_k(0) for every k ∈ ℕ with k ≥ |y|, so M = ⋃_{k∈ℕ} (M ∩ B_k(0)). For each k the ball B_k(0) is compact, so by admissibility θ is Hⁿ-integrable on M ∩ B_k(0); in particular θ is a.e.-strongly measurable for Hⁿ⌞(M ∩ B_k(0)). A function that is a.e.-strongly measurable for the restrictions of a measure to each of countably many sets is a.e.-strongly measurable for the restriction to their union (Mathlib aestronglyMeasurable_iUnion_iff). Hence θ is a.e.-strongly measurable, in particular a.e.-measurable, for Hⁿ⌞M; therefore ρ = ofReal ∘ θ is a.e.-measurable for Hⁿ⌞M (ofReal is measurable), and ρ(y) < ∞ for every y.

3. Proof of (i). Let K ⊆ E be compact; K is closed, hence Borel. By the formula for withDensity on measurable sets (withDensity_apply) and Measure.restrict_restrict, μ(K) = ∫⁻_K ρ d(Hⁿ⌞M) = ∫⁻_{K∩M} ofReal(θ) dHⁿ. Since ofReal(s) ≤ |s| for every real s, μ(K) ≤ ∫⁻_{K∩M} |θ| dHⁿ, and the right side is finite because θ is Hⁿ-integrable on M ∩ K = K ∩ M (admissibility with the compact set K). Thus μ(K) < ∞ for every compact K, i.e. μ is finite on compact sets.

4. A general identity. For a measure ν, a ν-a.e.-measurable density ρ: E → [0, ∞] with ρ < ∞ ν-a.e., and an arbitrary function h: E → ℝ, one has ∫ h d(ν.withDensity ρ) = ∫ ρ(y).toReal·h(y) dν(y) (Mathlib integral_withDensity_eq_integral_toReal_smul₀). This identity includes the fact that h is ν.withDensity ρ-integrable if and only if (ρ.toReal)·h is ν-integrable, so it is also valid when both Bochner integrals are 0 by the non-integrability convention.

5. Proof of (ii). Let g: E → ℝ be arbitrary. By step 1 and step 4 with ν := Hⁿ⌞M and the density ρ = ofReal ∘ θ (admissible by step 2): ∫ g dμ = ∫ (ofReal θ(y)).toReal·g(y) d(Hⁿ⌞M)(y).

6. Since M is Hⁿ-null-measurable, Hⁿ⌞M-almost every y lies in M (Mathlib ae_restrict_mem₀). For y ∈ M we have θ(y) > 0, hence (ofReal θ(y)).toReal = θ(y). So the integrands (ofReal θ(y)).toReal·g(y) and θ(y)·g(y) agree Hⁿ⌞M-almost everywhere, and their integrals with respect to Hⁿ⌞M coincide (integral_congr_ae). Therefore ∫ g dμ = ∫_M θ(y)·g(y) dHⁿ(y), which is (ii). ∎

subproblem.title: Upper density theorem: ν(A ∩ B_r(x))/rⁿ → 0 for Hⁿ-a.e. x outside A
subproblem.statement: Let n, ℓ ∈ ℕ, E := Ambient n ℓ = ℝ^{n+ℓ} with its Borel σ-algebra, Hⁿ := μHE[n], let ν be a measure on E that is finite on compact sets, and let A ⊆ E be a Borel set. Then for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ E: if x ∉ A, then ν(A ∩ B_r(x))/rⁿ → 0 as r ↓ 0, where B_r(x) is the closed ball and ν(A ∩ B_r(x)) is taken as a real number (ν.real = toReal ∘ ν; it is finite since B_r(x) is compact).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (ν : Measure (Ambient n ℓ)) (A : Set (Ambient n ℓ)), IsFiniteMeasureOnCompacts ν → MeasurableSet A → ∀ᵐ x ∂(μHE[n] : Measure (Ambient n ℓ)), x ∉ A → Tendsto (fun r : ℝ ↦ ν.real (A ∩ closedBall x r) / r ^ n) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 0)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: the upper density theorem quoted in the parent proof (Simon Ch. 1, Theorem 3.6), localized as in Simon Ch. 1, Remark 3.7(2) so that only finiteness of ν on compact sets is needed. No errata apply.

Notation. E := Ambient n ℓ, Hⁿ := μHE[n] on E, B_r(x) := closed ball, ball(x, r) := open ball, ν.real(S) := ν(S).toReal. ω := realUnitBallVolume n = ofReal(π^{n/2}/Γ(n/2 + 1)) (with n regarded as a real number ≥ 0); ω ∈ (0, ∞) by SimonGMT Chapter01.realUnitBallVolume_pos and realUnitBallVolume_ne_top (Γ > 0 on (0, ∞)).

1. Finite case. Let A' ⊆ E be Borel with ν(A') < ∞. We show: for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ E, if x ∉ A' then ν.real(A' ∩ B_r(x))/rⁿ → 0 as r ↓ 0.
(a) Let ν* := ν.toOuterMeasure (the outer measure underlying ν; ν*(S) = ν(S) for every set S, and ν* agrees with the measure on Borel sets). ν* is a Borel-regular outer measure (SimonGMT Chapter01.measure_toOuterMeasure_isBorelRegular: Borel sets are ν*-Carathéodory measurable by Mathlib le_toOuterMeasure_caratheodory, and every set S has a Borel superset of the same ν*-measure, e.g. a measurable hull). The Borel set A' is ν*-Carathéodory measurable, and ν*(A') = ν(A') < ∞.
(b) By the upper density theorem (Simon Ch. 1, 3.6; SimonGMT Chapter01.ae_dimensionalUpperDensity_eq_zero_outside, applied to the Borel-regular outer measure ν*, the dimension n ≥ 0 and the set A'), for simonHausdorffMeasureReal n-a.e. x: if x ∉ A' then limsup_{r↓0} D_x(r) = 0, where D_x(r) := ν*(A' ∩ B_r(x)) / (ω·ofReal(r)^n) ∈ [0, ∞] (this limsup along the right-neighbourhoods of 0 is SimonGMT's dimensionalUpperDensity ν* n A' x). By SimonGMT Chapter02.simonHausdorffMeasureReal_nat_eq_euclideanHausdorffMeasure, simonHausdorffMeasureReal n = μHE[n] = Hⁿ on E; so the statement holds for Hⁿ-a.e. x.
(c) Fix such an x with x ∉ A'. In [0, ∞] we have 0 ≤ liminf_{r↓0} D_x(r) ≤ limsup_{r↓0} D_x(r) = 0 (the filter of right-neighbourhoods of 0 is nontrivial and [0, ∞] is a complete lattice), so liminf = limsup = 0 and therefore D_x(r) → 0 as r ↓ 0 (tendsto_of_liminf_eq_limsup). Since toReal: [0, ∞] → ℝ is continuous at 0, D_x(r).toReal → 0, hence ω.toReal·D_x(r).toReal → 0.
(d) For r > 0 we have ofReal(r)^n = ofReal(rⁿ) ∈ (0, ∞), ω ∈ (0, ∞), and ν*(A' ∩ B_r(x)) = ν(A' ∩ B_r(x)) ≤ ν(A') < ∞. Hence D_x(r).toReal = ν.real(A' ∩ B_r(x))/(ω.toReal·rⁿ), i.e. ν.real(A' ∩ B_r(x))/rⁿ = ω.toReal·D_x(r).toReal. The two functions of r agree for every r > 0, so by (c) ν.real(A' ∩ B_r(x))/rⁿ → 0 as r ↓ 0.

2. Localization. For k ∈ ℕ let A_k := A ∩ ball(0, k). A_k is Borel, and ν(A_k) ≤ ν(B_k(0)) < ∞ because B_k(0) is compact and ν is finite on compact sets. By step 1 applied to A' := A_k there is an Hⁿ-null set Z_k such that for every x ∉ Z_k with x ∉ A_k: ν.real(A_k ∩ B_r(x))/rⁿ → 0 as r ↓ 0. The set Z := ⋃_{k∈ℕ} Z_k is Hⁿ-null, being a countable union of null sets (ae_all_iff).

3. Let x ∉ Z with x ∉ A. Choose k ∈ ℕ with k > |x| + 1. As x ∉ A we also have x ∉ A_k, so by step 2, ν.real(A_k ∩ B_r(x))/rⁿ → 0. For 0 < r < 1 and y ∈ B_r(x) we have |y| ≤ |x| + |y − x| ≤ |x| + r < |x| + 1 < k, so B_r(x) ⊆ ball(0, k) and therefore A ∩ B_r(x) = A_k ∩ B_r(x). Thus ν.real(A ∩ B_r(x))/rⁿ = ν.real(A_k ∩ B_r(x))/rⁿ for all r ∈ (0, 1); since (0, 1) belongs to the filter of right-neighbourhoods of 0, ν.real(A ∩ B_r(x))/rⁿ → 0 as r ↓ 0.

4. Step 3 holds for every x outside the Hⁿ-null set Z, which proves the claim. ∎

subproblem.title: Weighted blow-up at a point of a Lusin piece with vanishing excess densities
subproblem.statement: Let n, ℓ ∈ ℕ, E := Ambient n ℓ = ℝ^{n+ℓ}, Hⁿ := μHE[n], let a = (M, θ) be an admissible pair (RectifiablePair n ℓ) with weight μ := (mk a).weight, let N ⊆ E be Borel with Hⁿ(N) < ∞, K ⊆ E compact with K ⊆ M ∩ N, x ∈ K a point at which θ restricted to K is continuous (ContinuousWithinAt θ K x), f ∈ C_c(E, ℝ), and Γ, L ∈ ℝ. Assume (H1) Hⁿ(N ∩ B_ρ(x)) ≤ ofReal(Γρⁿ) for every ρ > 0; (H2) μ(Kᶜ ∩ B_r(x))/rⁿ → 0 as r ↓ 0; (H3) (Hⁿ⌞N)(Kᶜ ∩ B_r(x))/rⁿ → 0 as r ↓ 0; (H4) (tⁿ)⁻¹∫_N f(t⁻¹(y − x)) dHⁿ(y) → L as t ↓ 0. (B_r(x) is the closed ball, Kᶜ = E ∖ K, and the measures in (H2), (H3) are taken as real numbers via toReal.) Then (tⁿ)⁻¹∫ f(t⁻¹(y − x)) dμ(y) → θ(x)·L as t ↓ 0.

Source: step 7 of the parent proof (the four-term comparison at a good point; Simon Ch. 3, proof of Theorem 1.6 '⇒' together with Remark 1.8(1)). The good-point properties used there, namely (a'), (b'), the bound (3b), the limit (3a) of the sibling ts_piece_density_blowup and the continuity of θ on the Lusin piece, are here the hypotheses (H2), (H3), (H1), (H4) and ContinuousWithinAt θ K x. No errata apply.

Notation. E := Ambient n ℓ, Hⁿ := μHE[n], M := a.M, θ := a.θ, μ := (mk a).weight, B_r(x) := closed ball, Kᶜ := E ∖ K, μ.real(S) := μ(S).toReal. All integrals are Hⁿ-integrals unless μ is indicated. Uses the sibling ts_pwb_pair_weight_integral (applied to a): (W1) μ(K') < ∞ for every compact K' ⊆ E; (W2) ∫ h dμ = ∫_M θh dHⁿ for every function h: E → ℝ.

1. Constants of f. f is continuous with compact support, so there is m ≥ 0 with |f(z)| ≤ m for every z. The topological support of f is compact, hence bounded: there is C₀ with |z| ≤ C₀ for z ∈ tsupport f. Put R := max(C₀, 1) > 0; then f(z) = 0 whenever |z| > R (such z lies outside tsupport f).

2. Rescaled functions. For t > 0 put g_t(y) := f(t⁻¹(y − x)) and B_t := B_{Rt}(x). Then g_t is continuous, |g_t| ≤ m, and g_t(y) = 0 for every y ∉ B_t: if |y − x| > Rt then |t⁻¹(y − x)| = t⁻¹|y − x| > R.

3. Integrability (t > 0). (a) g_t is Hⁿ-integrable on N, since it is Borel, bounded by m, and Hⁿ(N) < ∞; hence it is also integrable on the subsets K and N ∖ K. (b) θ·g_t is Hⁿ-integrable on M: θ is Hⁿ-integrable on M ∩ B_t because B_t is compact (admissibility of a), and g_t is a bounded measurable function, so θ·g_t is integrable on M ∩ B_t; it vanishes on M ∖ B_t by step 2, and M is Hⁿ-null-measurable, so θ·g_t is integrable on M (IntegrableOn.of_ae_sdiff_eq_zero). Consequently θ·g_t is integrable on K ⊆ M, and so is (θ − θ(x))·g_t = θg_t − θ(x)g_t.

4. Decomposition (t > 0).
(a) ∫ g_t dμ = ∫_M θg_t, by (W2) with h = g_t.
(b) ∫_M θg_t = ∫_{M∩K} θg_t + ∫_{M∖K} θg_t, because K is Borel and θg_t is integrable on M (step 3(b)); and M ∩ K = K since K ⊆ M.
(c) ∫_{M∖K} θg_t = ∫_{Kᶜ} g_t dμ. Indeed, by (W2) with h = 1_{Kᶜ}·g_t: ∫_{Kᶜ} g_t dμ = ∫ 1_{Kᶜ}g_t dμ = ∫_M θ·1_{Kᶜ}g_t = ∫_M 1_{Kᶜ}·(θg_t) = ∫_{M∩Kᶜ} θg_t (Kᶜ is Borel), and M ∩ Kᶜ = M ∖ K.
(d) ∫_K θg_t = θ(x)∫_K g_t + ∫_K (θ − θ(x))g_t, by linearity (both integrands integrable on K by step 3).
(e) ∫_K g_t = ∫_N g_t − ∫_{N∖K} g_t, because K ⊆ N, K is Borel and g_t is integrable on N.
Combining (a)–(e) and multiplying by (tⁿ)⁻¹:
(tⁿ)⁻¹∫ g_t dμ = θ(x)·T₁(t) − θ(x)·T₂(t) + T₃(t) + T₄(t), where
T₁(t) := (tⁿ)⁻¹∫_N g_t, T₂(t) := (tⁿ)⁻¹∫_{N∖K} g_t, T₃(t) := (tⁿ)⁻¹∫_K (θ − θ(x))g_t, T₄(t) := (tⁿ)⁻¹∫_{Kᶜ} g_t dμ.

5. Rescaling the hypotheses. Since R > 0, the map t ↦ Rt sends (0, ∞) into (0, ∞) and tends to 0 as t → 0, so it maps the filter of right-neighbourhoods of 0 into itself. Hence (H2) and (H3) give Q_μ(Rt) → 0 and Q_N(Rt) → 0 as t ↓ 0, where Q_μ(r) := μ.real(Kᶜ ∩ B_r(x))/rⁿ and Q_N(r) := (Hⁿ⌞N).real(Kᶜ ∩ B_r(x))/rⁿ. Note that (tⁿ)⁻¹ = Rⁿ/(Rt)ⁿ for t > 0.

6. T₁(t) → L as t ↓ 0: T₁(t) is exactly the expression in (H4).

7. T₂(t) → 0. Fix t > 0. Since g_t = 0 on (N ∖ K) ∖ B_t, ∫_{N∖K} g_t = ∫_{(N∖K)∩B_t} g_t, and |∫_{(N∖K)∩B_t} g_t| ≤ m·Hⁿ.real((N ∖ K) ∩ B_t) (the set has finite measure, being contained in N). Since (N ∖ K) ∩ B_t = (Kᶜ ∩ B_t) ∩ N and Kᶜ ∩ B_t is Borel, Hⁿ((N ∖ K) ∩ B_t) = (Hⁿ⌞N)(Kᶜ ∩ B_t). Hence |T₂(t)| ≤ (tⁿ)⁻¹·m·(Hⁿ⌞N).real(Kᶜ ∩ B_{Rt}(x)) = mRⁿ·Q_N(Rt), which tends to 0 by step 5. So T₂(t) → 0.

8. T₄(t) → 0. Fix t > 0. Since g_t = 0 on Kᶜ ∖ B_t, ∫_{Kᶜ} g_t dμ = ∫_{Kᶜ∩B_t} g_t dμ, and μ(Kᶜ ∩ B_t) ≤ μ(B_t) < ∞ by (W1) (B_t is compact). Hence |T₄(t)| ≤ (tⁿ)⁻¹·m·μ.real(Kᶜ ∩ B_{Rt}(x)) = mRⁿ·Q_μ(Rt), which tends to 0 by step 5.

9. T₃(t) → 0. Let ε > 0 and put c := mRⁿ·max(Γ, 0) + 1 > 0. By continuity of θ restricted to K at x there is δ > 0 such that |θ(y) − θ(x)| < ε/c for every y ∈ K with |y − x| < δ. Let 0 < t < δ/R, so that Rt < δ. Since g_t = 0 off B_t, ∫_K (θ − θ(x))g_t = ∫_{K∩B_t} (θ − θ(x))g_t, and for y ∈ K ∩ B_t we have |y − x| ≤ Rt < δ, hence |(θ(y) − θ(x))g_t(y)| ≤ (ε/c)·m. Moreover, as K ⊆ N, (H1) with ρ := Rt > 0 gives Hⁿ(K ∩ B_t) ≤ Hⁿ(N ∩ B_t) ≤ ofReal(Γ(Rt)ⁿ) < ∞, so Hⁿ.real(K ∩ B_t) ≤ max(Γ(Rt)ⁿ, 0) ≤ max(Γ, 0)·(Rt)ⁿ. Therefore |T₃(t)| ≤ (tⁿ)⁻¹·(ε/c)·m·max(Γ, 0)·(Rt)ⁿ = (ε/c)·mRⁿmax(Γ, 0) = ε(c − 1)/c < ε for all t ∈ (0, δ/R). As ε > 0 was arbitrary, T₃(t) → 0.

10. Conclusion. By steps 6–9, θ(x)T₁(t) − θ(x)T₂(t) + T₃(t) + T₄(t) → θ(x)L − θ(x)·0 + 0 + 0 = θ(x)L as t ↓ 0. By step 4 this expression equals (tⁿ)⁻¹∫ f(t⁻¹(y − x)) dμ(y) for every t > 0, i.e. on a set belonging to the filter of right-neighbourhoods of 0. Hence (tⁿ)⁻¹∫ f(t⁻¹(y − x)) dμ(y) → θ(x)·L as t ↓ 0. (The hypothesis x ∈ K is not needed for this argument; it is kept because it holds in the application, where ContinuousWithinAt θ K x is obtained from continuity of θ on K.) ∎
